methods.label: Pair the terms in the running sum
methods.explanation:
Instruction 2 increases \(X\) before instruction 3 adds it to \(S\). Thus the numbers added are \(5,7,9,\ldots\), rather than starting at \(3\).

Find the running sum when \(X=199\). The sum
\[
5+7+9+\cdots+199
\]
has
\[
\frac{199-5}{2}+1=98
\]
terms. Pair the first with the last, the second with the next-to-last, and so on. Each pair has sum \(204\), and there are \(49\) pairs, so
\[
S=49\cdot204=9996<10000.
\]
Every added term is positive, so the program could not have stopped on an earlier pass. On the next pass, \(X\) becomes \(201\) and
\[
S=9996+201=10197\ge10000.
\]
Instruction 5 therefore prints \(201\), choice \(\mathrm{E}\).
methods.levelReason: The method follows the ordered updates and sums equally spaced terms by pairing. Positivity and two consecutive checks establish the first stopping point.
